draftContext.markdown:
**Core #584 status unknown.** This is the base of the entire Fleet Runner NAS integration stack (#586 stacks on it, #588 stacks on #586, and BookcaseDiscovery #90/#91/#92 and core #589/#590/#591 all block downstream). The article does not have evidence of why #584 is unmerged — no review hold, failing test, or open design question is documented. Owner gate: someone with repository access needs to report the actual status of #584 before the Fleet Runner thread can be meaningfully prioritized.

**Core #590 ADR is unnumbered and unregistered.** `draft-nas-tenant-identity-model.md` is in Proposed status and not in the ADR registry. Core #589 (authenticated input delivery) and BookcaseDiscovery #90 (NAS worker profile) are drafted against this identity model. These PRs cannot merge with an unresolved identity architecture. Owner gate: ADR review and registry assignment.

**NS-5 real-degraded-tier capture gap.** Zero cases against a minimum of 14. Duration of a qualifying capture session is unknown from available evidence. Owner gate: schedule a capture session on a non-Pro device and determine whether this is a days or weeks problem before treating NS-10/NS-11 as anything other than parked.

**Stale article review PRs.** daily-logger #526 (2026-11-03 article), #529 (2026-11-04), #530 (2026-11-05) are open draft with no documented disposition. Owner gate: merge, close, or document the process gap.

**Telemetry cutover blocker unknown.** Core #587, morning-cockpit #61, daily-logger #531 have been open draft with the stream frozen since 2026-05-12. No documented blocker in available evidence. Owner gate: identify what is preventing the cutover PRs from progressing.

**Restore drill scope clarification.** `restore-drill` restores to a temp directory and verifies hash integrity against the manifest. It does not perform a live database swap. Whether the drill has been executed against real production data (as opposed to test fixtures) is not documented in available evidence. The test suite passes, but a backup that has only been drilled against synthetic data carries residual restore risk.

**mtime/size skip heuristic trust boundary.** The append-only and immutability properties of data-root files are enforced by code contract in the write paths, not filesystem permissions. This is a documented trust boundary. No evidence of a formal audit of all write paths that touch these files.

**core #585 and workstation-yuri #11** are open, non-draft, non-critical-path. No disposition documented.
